assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defines a physiological hormone axis (proglucagon-derived GLP-1, its insulinotropic and satiety actions) and carries it through to therapies that transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity treatment. Originality, clarity and breadth of clinical impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst's physiology and human studies, Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) form, and Drucker's work on GLP-1 biology and the gut hormone axis form a coherent three-person configuration. Knudsen's drug-development role is real but industrial; other early contributors such as Habener are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, large outcome trials and widespread clinical use; recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Mojsov, Habener-group work, Holst, Drucker and the drug developers is contested.
I am relying on my own recollection of the history and have not verified details of priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of a new intracellular signaling logic from ER to nucleus (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing, unconventional mRNA processing), with deep relevance to proteostasis, secretory cell biology and disease. Conceptually clean and highly original; it also speaks to RNA processing as a regulatory mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Walter's lab defined the pathway components and IRE1 mechanism; Mori's work established the signaling and transcriptional program. Two laureates is a natural fit, with possible but weaker claims from others in the field.
assessment.maturity: Fundamental mechanism confirmed repeatedly over three decades; therapeutic translation is still emerging but is not required for a fundamental discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views it as sufficiently disease-linked for Physiology or Medicine.
Allocation to secondary contributors in the pathway is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin and the framing of nutrient-responsive growth control as a conserved kinase pathway. It has wide influence on cell growth, metabolism, aging and cancer, with clear originality.
assessment.attribution: Hall's discovery of TOR in yeast is the decisive foundational step. Later mTOR complex biochemistry (Sabatini, Schreiber and others) is important, but I would not include Sabatini given unresolved credit and conduct questions, so a single laureate is the cleanest configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed and widely used; clinical use of rapalogs and mTOR inhibitors supports maturity, though some translational promises have been modest.
uncertainties: Whether a single-laureate prize is acceptable versus including mTOR-complex contributors.
Credit for the original rapamycin target identification in mammals is shared among several groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, a conceptually new class of living drugs. Impact on cancer treatment and cell engineering is large and documented.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June established costimulatory CAR designs and led key clinical translation; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T-cell trials. Eshhar and others earlier made the first-generation CAR, who are not in the credited list, which complicates a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Approved products and long-term follow-up exist; toxicities, access and solid-tumour limits remain, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Priority of first-generation CAR work and the role of Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy versus CAR design itself.
Long-term durability and safety data are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proof that inhibiting a single causative oncogenic kinase (BCR-ABL) turns a fatal leukemia into a manageable chronic disease; the paradigm of targeted cancer therapy. Clear, original and of lasting clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Lydon's chemistry and compound program, Druker's clinical development and Sawyers' resistance mechanisms and second-line inhibitors are separable, defensible contributions. The earlier discovery of the BCR-ABL fusion (Rowley, Groffen and others) is outside this credited list.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of survival data and independent confirmation; recognition is well past due, which could argue it has already been honored in the community by other prizes.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should reach back to the underlying BCR-ABL discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanism-guided antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 splicing leading to nusinersen, an effective therapy for a previously lethal childhood neurodegenerative disease. As an RNA processing scientist I regard the splicing logic as elegant and a direct, validated therapeutic principle.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing regulatory elements and the ISS-N1 target concept; Bennett led the antisense chemistry and drug development. Hua, Singh and others also contributed experimental work, which makes a clean allocation of credit harder.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with multi-year follow-up; confirmation is strong, though timing could be premature relative to other candidates on the list.
uncertainties: Role of other groups in identifying the SMN2 target sequence and optimizing the oligonucleotide.
Whether the committee prefers recognising the antisense platform as a whole.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING reveals how cytosolic DNA is sensed and converted into innate immune signaling through the second messenger cGAMP, with consequences for infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and senescence. Original and highly generative.
assessment.attribution: Chen's identification of cGAS and cGAMP is the decisive biochemical step; Barber's discovery of STING is also decisive. Others such as Ishikawa, Sun and Wu are credited but are more naturally treated as co-discoverers within the Chen and Barber labs.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is robust and well confirmed; therapeutic translation is early and still unproven.
uncertainties: Credit split between STING discovery and cGAS discovery, and the contributions of Ishikawa and Sun.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Channelrhodopsin and its adaptation as a genetically targeted tool allowed causal control of defined cell populations. It has transformed experimental physiology, particularly neuroscience, though disease-level impact is mostly indirect.
assessment.attribution: The microbial rhodopsin work of Nagel, Hegemann and Bamberg, and the neuronal adaptation by Boyden and Deisseroth, along with Miesenböck's earlier genetic photostimulation, makes credit very crowded. Three names is a compromise and any choice excludes defensible claimants.
assessment.maturity: Technique is well replicated and ubiquitous, but impact is as a tool; clinical applications (e.g. vision restoration) are only emerging.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among six candidates is deeply contested.
Method versus discovery: whether it fits the prize's emphasis on physiology or medicine.
